description: A CTO must approve the execution plan for a large machine-learning evaluation run, deciding GPU capacity, workload isolation, instance purchasing mode, completion timing, and cost tracking with input from the ML platform lead and FinOps analyst.

shared_context.S1: The company plans to run the Atlas model evaluation in the cloud next week.
shared_context.S2: Morgan makes the binding decision on the infrastructure plan and its associated commitments.
shared_context.S3: The current draft reserves 8 GPUs from the shared pool, uses a mix of spot and on-demand instances, and targets completion by Friday morning.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal infrastructure approval process, Morgan checks with the ML platform and FinOps owners before approving the run.
shared_context.S5: Morgan may approve the infrastructure plan after consulting the ML platform owner and the FinOps owner.
shared_context.S6: The infrastructure approval record includes the workload's data-handling choice and any required cost controls.
shared_context.S7: The 18-hour duration in a FinOps cost estimate is a billing assumption independent of the completion deadline; the estimate can be used for approval without deriving a start time from the Wednesday 06:00 UTC target.
shared_context.S8: The infrastructure approval policy allows approval after the plan has been reviewed by the relevant owners; administrative follow-up, including updating the infrastructure request or posting the cost-center tag, may be completed after approval.

PF1.text: While preparing the evaluation input this afternoon, Leah confirmed that three customer-labeled datasets are included. They must run in an isolated cloud account rather than the shared GPU pool, and the measured workload needs exactly 12 GPUs to finish by Wednesday 06:00 UTC; she has not updated the infrastructure request because the data-preparation review is still open.

PF2.text: Owen's billing review this morning confirmed that running exactly 12 GPUs on fully on-demand instances for the planned 18-hour window will cost $4,320 and remain under the approved $5,000 evaluation budget; he has not added the cost-center tag or posted the calculation because the invoice export arrived only an hour ago.

acceptance_conditions: The run must reserve exactly 12 GPUs.
The run must use fully on-demand instances.
The customer-labeled datasets must run in an isolated cloud account.
The run must target completion by Wednesday 06:00 UTC.
A commitment whose detail requires adding or posting a cost-center tag for the Atlas evaluation must exist.

content_checks.C2: 'on-demand' in decisions['instance_mode'] and 'spot' not in decisions['instance_mode']
content_checks.C5: any('cost-center tag' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The visible draft calls for 8 shared-pool GPUs and Friday completion; PF1 changes the required capacity to exactly 12, requires an isolated account, and changes the target to Wednesday 06:00 UTC.

The visible draft allows a mix of spot and on-demand instances and contains no tagging commitment; PF2 changes the instance choice to fully on-demand and requires a commitment whose detail mentions adding or posting the cost-center tag after confirming the $4,320 cost is within the $5,000 budget.
